t: Forty gold on Hessle's board for the Web Gulch ettercap. Up ten since it snared a lad.
Forty gold for the cloaker in the guano mine's deep gallery. Nobody knows who posted it.
The cloaker's forty on the board, fifty at Marta's, a hundred by the third round at the Hex.
Nobody has ever collected on the cloaker.
Thirty silver at the lantern house frees a slave. No questions asked, either way.
Nobody bothers the dwarves. Not since the Water Burning.
New-moon card at the Hex: five silver to fight, winner keeps ten.
A stranger's five is fronted by the crowd, never the bar. Lose it and catch hell.
Thirty in your box behind the southeast bar and you walk to the lantern a free man.
When a fighter dies, his box buys the house a round. The room drinks his freedom.
Talmok's the champion. Greataxe on the road, fists in the pit. He opens reckless.
The gnolls have gone Snoot: their king's dead at the moot, and the Dominion was there.
Gnolls don't usually range north of Web Gulch. But the Snoot's trouble creeps upward.
The harvest houses are hiring mercs and fighting slaves to guard their shipments.
When the Weigh-House lamp burns past the fourth bell, the scales are lit.
Dose-work across the water: a silver the thimble above the wet, three below it.
Keep your lamp out of Mouths One and Six after dark. The House has no second morning.
Locals say 'the galleries' for the east workings and 'the guano mine' for the bat caves. Say 'Guano Galleries' and they know you're not from here.
The guano mine pays eight copper a day on the scrape, three silver a giant-bat head.
Don't touch the roost at the guano mine: no fire, no smoke, no nets, no shouting.
Halfway Lake: knee-deep forty paces out, then it drops. Nothing off the point comes up.
The Coldridge route, that's what locals call the road up to the Doors. Marko's father's caravan was lost on it.
Brennock's maps tell which shafts run safe, which run wet, and which are watched.
Warrens Pete says six came up. He says six a little too fast.
Old Hob, about the doors down past the wet: they're not locked, they're promised.
The landlord in the deepest pool showed you, in pictures, what comes down the stream: fungal light, and clacking.
Ambrose Winters on Fountain Street. Acquisitions and Estates. Ran with Pyronimus and Tarlyn in the Orc War, they say. Won't deal with thieves if he can help it.
Down the road past the fork: Web Gulch. Silk-cutters work it at noon, when the spiders sulk. They pay a boy to drum.
Seventeen miles down, the Halfway Inn: the only well on the road.
Night crews pumped the Warrens' water stair dry, three nights running, and cut the warranted door at the foot of it. The one law. The scales are lit.
